summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would establish Renew Australia as a public authority to plan the electricity system's transition to renewable energy and support affected workers and communities.
The authority could build, finance, own or operate renewable energy projects, run reverse auctions for private projects and plan the closure of coal-fired power stations.
Its substantive provisions would begin on proclamation or, if no date were set, after six months, with project decisions required to serve the public interest.
changes: A board and chief executive would be established to govern the authority.
Law reform recommendations, accompanied by draft legislation, would be due within 12 months of commencement.
Borrowing from outside the Commonwealth would require the Treasurer's written approval.
The Treasurer could guarantee the authority's external borrowings.
summary.affected: Fossil fuel power stations being phased out, clean energy companies building renewable energy plants, and workers and communities affected by the phase out are affected.
